newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares edge up in jittery trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares edge up in jittery trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices edged up in low-key trading on Monday as trepid investors slowed down the market's 20-day long romp into record territory and settled for smaller deals, brokers said.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said in a report its all-share index rose 0.22 percent to 419.19 points, a far cry from the five percent increases of the past weeks. Monday's level was the 20th highest level for the index in as many trading days.
Turnover was an average 64.8 million pounds ($19 million).
"People are getting worried about all these rises. They're waiting for the bubble to burst, for the correction that will come," said Walid el-Kholi of El-Rashad Securities Brokerage.
The CMAindex has risen 41 percent from its levels at the beginning of the year, compared to a 39.3 percent increase for the whole of 1996.
Investors continued to target the popular cement and milling shares despite the slackened pace but several other individual stocks performed well.

Medinet Nasr Housing and Development continued to dominate trading in what brokers said were a series of "marriage" transactions where large shareholders sell their holdings to each other. The shares rose 12 pounds to 486 after shares worth 15.8 million pounds ($4.65 million) changed hands.
Large deals in Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN also boosted the stock's turnover to 6.1 million but share prices fell 8.5 pounds to 163.5.
Suez Cement was also actively traded, with shares rising 0.2 to 80. Amriyah Cement was also busy but shares fell 1.75 to 88.25.
Foreign interest in Abu Qir Fertiliser and Chemical Industries and Misr Chemical Industries stirred up trade in the stocks and firmed prices.

Misr Chemical closed 1.35 up at 29.05 while Abu Qir ended 5.6 higher to 117.68. Brokers said that there was talk that the fertiliser firm would soon change its by-laws to allow foreigners to own shares or face suspension from the bourse.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 717.41 points from 707.55 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 271.33 points from 272.97 points.
Out of the 83 shares traded, 46 gained, 23 lost and 14 ended the day unchanged.
